**Current stage:** Framework/bootstrap implementation exists and local fixture tests pass. The project is **not yet ready for production integration or production deployment**.

# 3. Important: Do Not Fill All Production Values Yet

Do **not** begin by replacing all 187 `<TBD>` values.

The current code still has implementation gaps that should be corrected first.

Filling the YAML today will not turn all modules into working live integrations.

Several collectors/executors currently operate only on test fixtures or explicitly block live access.

The correct sequence is:

```text

Controlled integration testing

        ↓
UAT
        ↓
Production
```

# 5. Step 1 — Ask CODEX to Complete the Core Framework First

Before any real Portainer/RabbitMQ/SSH/Recording connection, CODEX should correct the following issues found in the generated project.

## 5.1 Wire the HTML Review UI

The current review templates display:

```text
SAVE NOTES
FINAL CONFIRMATION
```

but these buttons are not wired to the existing API endpoints.

The current textareas also do not reliably load/save their persisted values through the page.

CODEX must implement:

- SAVE NOTES from the central review page.
- module-note saving.
- result-note saving.
- Splunk-dashboard-note saving.
- general-note saving if enabled.
- reload persisted notes into textareas.
- FINAL CONFIRMATION UI.
- explicit APPROVE / REJECT decision.
- confirmation handling.
- success/error feedback.
- prevention of finalization when required review conditions are missing.
- tests of the actual UI/API flow.

Do not rely only on direct Python calls in integration tests.

---

## 5.2 Validate Note Targets

The current note API accepts IDs from the request.

Before production, CODEX must ensure:

```text
result_id belongs to the specified run
dashboard_id exists in configured Splunk dashboards
module is a valid configured module
run is in a state where notes may be changed
```

A result from another run must never be attachable to the current run.

---

## 5.3 Integrate Real Module Evidence

The Evidence Manager exists, but normal module execution currently does not write the module evidence described by the specification.

CODEX must connect collectors/orchestrator to evidence storage so modules can persist, for example:

```text
Portainer raw API JSON
RabbitMQ queues/exchanges/bindings JSON
SSH stdout/stderr
df output
NFS output
chrony output
DB stdout/stderr
Recording screenshots
Recording trace
Recording backend evidence
normalized result JSON
```

Each stored item should have:

```text
run_id
module
site
result/check association where appropriate
path
checksum
MIME/type
timestamp
```

Evidence must be linked from the review UI.

---

## 5.4 Complete Snapshot Summaries

The current snapshot code writes:

```text
site_summaries: []
module_summaries: []
```

even though summary functions exist.

CODEX must populate:

```text
Site 1 status
Site 2 status
module summaries
parity summaries
overall automation status
```

and include them in the frozen snapshot and final report.

---

## 5.5 Replace the Basic PDF Renderer

The current PDF implementation is only a minimal single-page PDF writer.

It is not sufficient for a real Weekend Report containing many results, notes, evidence references, and multiple sites.

CODEX must implement a production-capable multi-page final report.

The final PDF must contain at least:

```text
cover / report header
RUN_ID
run timestamps
application version
Git commit
configuration revision/hash
overall status
Site 1 summary
Site 2 summary
module summaries
Portainer details + notes
DOCTOR details + notes
RabbitMQ details + notes
Recording functional + cleanup details + notes
Infrastructure details + notes
Database details + notes
Splunk dashboard-by-dashboard notes
result-specific notes
reviewer identity
APPROVE/REJECT decision
confirmation timestamp
evidence/reference appendix
```

It must paginate correctly.

The PDF must render from the frozen snapshot only.

---

## 5.6 Implement Real Authentication/Authorization Boundary

Current reviewer resolution is development-only:

```text
X-Reviewer header
or
WEEKEND_REPORT_DEV_REVIEWER
or
anonymous
```

That is acceptable only for local development.

Before production CODEX must support an organization-approved identity model.

At minimum, the design must distinguish:

```text
development mode
production authenticated mode
```

Production must not allow a caller to impersonate a reviewer by sending an arbitrary header.

Also add authorization for:

```text
start run
save review notes
finalize report
view protected evidence
```

Add CSRF protection where browser/session authentication requires it.

---

## 5.7 Fix PostgreSQL Run-Lock Semantics

The current SQLite transaction path serializes local tests, but the PostgreSQL path should explicitly protect the singleton `run_lock` row.

CODEX should use an atomic PostgreSQL locking strategy such as:

```sql
SELECT ...
FROM run_lock
WHERE name = 'weekend_report'
FOR UPDATE;
```

inside the run-creation transaction.

Add a real PostgreSQL concurrency test proving:

```text
two simultaneous create requests
        ↓
exactly one active run created
```

Also test multiple workers claiming one CREATED run.

---

## 5.8 Implement Stale Worker / Recovery Policy

Heartbeat exists, but a complete stale-run recovery policy is not implemented.

Define and implement:

```text
heartbeat timeout
how stale RUNNING runs are detected
when a run becomes FAILED
when RECOVERY_REQUIRED is used
how the lock is released
how current_module is preserved
```

Recording must receive special treatment.

Never blindly restart a stale Recording step because the previous worker may have created a synthetic object before crashing.

---

## 5.9 Fix Docker Environment/Secret Handling

Current `deploy/docker/compose.yml` uses:

```text
env_file: ./env.example
```

and PostgreSQL currently has a default:

```text
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-<TBD>}
```

This should not be the production behavior.

CODEX should change the model to:

```text
env.example
    = documentation/template only

real .env or approved secret injection
    = runtime values
```

Docker must fail clearly if required production secrets are missing.

Do not allow a container to start using literal `<TBD>` as a password.

Do not commit the real `.env`.

---

# 6. Exact First Prompt to Give CODEX

Use the following for the next CODEX session:

```text
Inspect the complete existing weekend-report repository before changing anything.

Do NOT begin production integrations yet.

The initial bootstrap is useful, but I need you to complete and harden the core framework before I fill the real production validation configuration.

Implement and test all of the following:

1. Wire the HTML review UI to the existing note APIs:
   - module notes
   - result notes
   - per-Splunk-dashboard notes
   - general notes if enabled
   - SAVE NOTES
   - reload persisted notes
   - FINAL CONFIRMATION
   - explicit APPROVE/REJECT

2. Validate note ownership:
   - result_id must belong to run_id
   - dashboard_id must exist in configured dashboards
   - module must be valid
   - notes can only be modified in an allowed run state.

3. Integrate the EvidenceManager into normal module execution. Every collector/check must be able to persist raw evidence and normalized evidence with checksum metadata and expose it through the review UI.

4. Populate real site_summaries and module_summaries in the frozen review snapshot. Include parity summaries as required.

5. Replace the current minimal single-page PDF writer with a production-capable multi-page final PDF renderer that includes the complete frozen report: run/code/config metadata, overall/site/module results, expected/actual findings, all reviewer notes, all Splunk notes, reviewer decision, timestamp, and evidence references.

6. Add a clean development-vs-production authentication boundary. Do not allow arbitrary X-Reviewer identity in production. Keep the production auth provider configurable because the organization-approved mechanism is still TBD.

7. Correct PostgreSQL concurrency semantics for run creation using an explicit database row-lock/atomic strategy and add PostgreSQL concurrency tests for duplicate run prevention and single worker claim.

8. Implement a documented stale-worker/recovery policy. Do not automatically replay a possibly state-changing Recording operation.

9. Fix Docker secret/environment handling:
   - env.example is a template only
   - no service may use literal <TBD> as a runtime secret
   - real runtime secrets come from a non-committed .env / Docker secret / approved secret mechanism
   - missing required secrets must fail clearly.

10. Add tests for every fix above.

11. Run:
   - config fixture validation
   - expected-invalid production template validation
   - unit tests
   - integration tests
   - ruff
   - mypy
   - pip-audit
   - Docker Compose config validation
   - Docker build if Docker is available
   - safe Compose smoke if Docker is available

12. Update docs/PROJECT_BUILD_REPORT.md with exactly what changed, what passed, what remains blocked, and what environment information I need next.

Do not invent production URLs, credentials, replica counts, RabbitMQ topology, thresholds, servers, NTP values, Splunk URLs, DB semantics, or Recording values.
Do not enable any state-changing Recording call.
Commit the completed hardening work as a separate Git commit.
```

Do this before supplying real production integration credentials.

# 9. Step 4 — Portainer First

Portainer should be the first real automated external integration.

Why:

- read-only,
- clear expected state,
- API-based,
- lower operational risk than Recording,
- good test of two-site validation/parity architecture.

## 9.1 Supply Configuration

Complete:

```text
config/portainer_expected.yml
```

and runtime environment variables for:

```text
PORTAINER_SITE1_URL
PORTAINER_SITE1_TOKEN
PORTAINER_SITE2_URL
PORTAINER_SITE2_TOKEN
```

Define:

```text
Portainer version
API contract
endpoint/environment IDs
TLS policy
timeouts
service names
expected replicas
healthy replica requirements
image policy if needed
required/optional services
parity fields
```

Treat the current repository as:

```text
GOOD IMPLEMENTATION FOUNDATION
```

not:

```text
FINISHED PRODUCTION AUTOMATION
```

